name: Isolated Partial Cerebellar Vermis Agenesis
aliases: Partial Agenesis of the Cerebellar Vermis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Neuroimaging-based Diagnostic Criteria for Cerebellar Vermis Agenesis

criteria.description: Neuroimaging evidence (MRI) demonstrating partial agenesis or hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis
Absence of other major brain malformations on neuroimaging
Presence of cerebellar dysfunction signs such as ataxia or dysmetria
Exclusion of syndromic or genetic conditions known to cause cerebellar vermis agenesis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Neuroimaging confirmation of partial cerebellar vermis agenesis with isolated cerebellar involvement and clinical evidence of cerebellar dysfunction
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on high-resolution MRI and clinical correlation; genetic testing may be used to exclude syndromic etiologies.

pathognomonic.notes: Impaired coordination of trunk movements typical in cerebellar vermis agenesis
Unsteady, wide-based gait due to cerebellar dysfunction
Inability to control the range of movement, especially on finger-to-nose testing

common.notes: Reduced muscle tone often observed in infants and young children
Involuntary eye movements due to cerebellar involvement

occasional.notes: Slurred or slow speech due to cerebellar dysfunction
Mild to moderate intellectual disability reported in some cases

rare.notes: Rarely associated with secondary ventricular enlargement
Irritability or hyperactivity in some patients

imaging: MRI demonstrating partial agenesis or hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis
Absence of other brain malformations on MRI
genetic: Exclusion of mutations associated with syndromic cerebellar malformations
other: Clinical cerebellar signs including ataxia and dysmetria

distinguishingFeatures: Complete or near-complete agenesis of cerebellar vermis with cystic dilatation of the fourth ventricle
Multisystem involvement including retinal dystrophy and renal disease

references: Parisi MA. Cerebellar malformations: clinical and molecular features. Neurogenetics. 2009;10(3):181-190.
Barkovich AJ, et al. Classification system for malformations of cortical development. Neurology. 2012;79(10):1039-1047.
